nary_nodes.label: Analysis of toddler foods
evidence: Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed, according to research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No existing event type matches a research analysis; mint new subclass of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Presentation of findings
evidence: “We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed,” said Hudson, who presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event in which findings or information are formally presented to an audience.

nary_nodes.label: FDA proposed front‑of‑package labeling rule

evidence: Prior research published in January found over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives that emerging research has linked to inflammation and disruptions in the gut microbiome.

nary_nodes.label: 80% of toddler foods are ultraprocessed

“The answer is over 80% of the products are ultraprocessed,” Hudson said.

nary_nodes.label: Nearly half of toddler foods failed WHO nutrition benchmark
evidence: Nearly half of those items also failed to meet at least one nutritional benchmark for children set by the World Health Organization.

nary_nodes.label: Many toddler foods high in sugar and sodium
evidence: “Many of them are high in sugar, high in sodium, but parents really cannot tell that from just walking down the aisle.”

nary_nodes.label: Products failing WHO sugar standards four times as likely ultraprocessed
evidence: “We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed,” said Hudson, who presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.

nary_nodes.label: Almost a quarter of foods higher in sodium than recommended
evidence: “Almost a quarter of the foods were higher in sodium than is recommended, and some were high in fat and calorie dense,” she added.

nary_nodes.label: Ultraprocessed foods crowd out healthier options
evidence: “The problem isn’t just what’s in these high-sugar, high-salt ultraprocessed foods, it’s what they crowd out,” said Jane Houlihan, research director for Healthy Babies Bright Futures, an alliance of nonprofits, scientists and donors with a mission of reducing babies’ exposures to neurotoxic chemicals.

nary_nodes.label: Toddler eating snack foods likely eats fewer whole grains etc.
evidence: “A toddler who fills up on fruit snacks, sweetened yogurt, crackers and snack bars is likely to eat fewer whole grains, vegetables, beans and other healthier foods,” Houlihan said in an email.

nary_nodes.label: Parents cannot tell ultraprocessed nature by aisle
evidence: “Many of them are high in sugar, high in sodium, but parents really cannot tell that from just walking down the aisle.”

nary_nodes.label: Industry markets toddler foods as healthy but not true
evidence: “Industry has marketed this toddler foods to make parents believe these foods were created for the health of toddlers, and it’s just not true.”

nary_nodes.label: No universal definition of ultraprocessed food
evidence: There is currently no universally accepted scientific definition of the term ‘ultraprocessed’ food, a spokesperson said.
